introduction-the-staging-bottleneck.core: A single shared QA environment is a queue: only one change can be tested at a time, and changes collide. On-demand environments give each PR its own stack, built from infrastructure-as-code.

first_principles.problem: Teams wait days for 'their turn' on staging, and tests break because of others' half-deployed changes.
derivation: Keep the **long-lived foundation** (cluster, network) shared.
Make the **per-PR layer** (namespace, release, DB) ephemeral.
Automate with **Terraform and Helm**.
Give each one a **URL** and clean it up.

analogy.title: A single office bathroom
analogy.story: Everyone queues for one room; on-demand environments give everyone their own.
analogy.breaks: Cost and data seeding are the main challenges.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: QA throughput scales with the number of PRs.

check.q: What's the main benefit of on-demand environments?
check.a: Parallel, isolated testing of every change without waiting for a shared environment.

the-architecture-terraform-vs-helm.core: Split the infrastructure in two. Terraform manages the slow-changing foundation (VPC, cluster, DNS zone, wildcard certificate, shared DB server). Helm deploys the fast, per-PR application layer into a namespace in seconds.

first_principles.problem: Creating a whole cluster per PR with Terraform takes 20 minutes and costs a fortune.
truths: Infrastructure layers change at different rates.
Cluster creation is slow; namespace creation is fast.
derivation: **Terraform**: foundation, applied rarely.
**Helm**: a release per PR into namespace `pr-N`.
Use Terraform for **per-PR cloud resources** only when needed (a DB on a shared server, a bucket).
Pass **outputs** (endpoints) into Helm values.

analogy.title: Building a mall vs. setting up pop-up stalls
analogy.story: The mall (foundation) is built once; stalls (PR environments) go up and come down in minutes.
analogy.breaks: Per-PR cloud resources through Terraform need state per environment (workspaces or state keys).

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: An environment is ready in about 60 seconds.

code.text:
# foundation exists (terraform apply once)
helm upgrade --install web-pr-412 ./chart -n pr-412 --create-namespace \
  --set image.tag=$SHA --set ingress.host=pr-412.preview.acme.dev

check.q: Why not create a full cluster per PR?
check.a: It's slow and expensive. A namespace on a shared cluster is created in seconds.

dynamic-routing-the-magic-url.core: A wildcard DNS record (*.preview.acme.dev) points at the ingress controller, and a wildcard TLS certificate covers it. Each PR's ingress claims pr-N.preview.acme.dev, so every PR gets a working HTTPS URL with no per-PR DNS changes.

first_principles.problem: Creating DNS records and certificates per PR is slow and hits rate limits.
derivation: Create **\*.preview.acme.dev → ingress LB** once (Terraform).
Issue a **wildcard cert** (cert-manager DNS-01).
Each Helm release sets **ingress.host = pr-N...**.
The ingress controller **routes by Host**.

analogy.title: An apartment building with a single street address
analogy.story: The street address gets mail to the building, and the unit number on each letter routes it to the right apartment.
analogy.breaks: Cookies and OAuth callback URLs may need wildcard support too.

example.title: Ingress for a PR

code.text:
ingress:
  host: pr-412.preview.acme.dev
  tls:
    - hosts: ["*.preview.acme.dev"]
      secretName: preview-wildcard-tls

example.outcome: every PR gets a clickable, secure URL.

check.q: Why use a wildcard certificate for previews?
check.a: One certificate covers every PR subdomain, avoiding per-PR issuance delays and rate limits.

lifecycle-management-the-cleanup.core: Forgotten environments bankrupt you. Destroy on PR close, set TTLs, run a scheduled reaper for orphans, and reconcile environments against the list of open PRs.

first_principles.problem: Fifty environments a week with missed teardowns means hundreds running after a quarter.
truths: Reconciliation beats relying on events alone.
derivation: On **PR closed** → helm uninstall + delete the namespace (+ terraform destroy).
Add a **TTL label**; the reaper deletes expired ones.
**Reconcile**: list namespaces vs open PRs and delete the extras.
**Alert** on environment count and cost.

analogy.title: Rental car returns
analogy.story: Returned cars are checked in, and a nightly audit finds any car whose rental ended but was never returned.
analogy.breaks: Aggressive reaping can kill environments people still need, so allow extensions via labels.

example.title: Reconciliation job
example.scenario: Delete namespaces whose PRs are closed.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Orphans can't survive more than a day.

code.text:
open=$(gh pr list --state open --json number -q '.[].number' | sed 's/^/pr-/')
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -l preview=true -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do
  echo "$open" | grep -qx "$ns" || kubectl delete ns "$ns"
done

check.q: Why reconcile against open PRs instead of relying only on close events?
check.a: Close events can be missed, and reconciliation catches every orphan regardless.

posting-the-preview-url-back-to-the-pr.core: An environment nobody can find is useless. Post the preview URL (and status) as a PR comment or GitHub deployment, update it on each push, and mark it inactive on teardown.

first_principles.problem: Reviewers don't know a preview exists, or which URL matches which PR.
truths: Reviewers live in the PR UI.
Deployments API shows environment links natively.
derivation: Create or update a **sticky comment** with the URL.
Or use the **GitHub Deployments API** (environment URL shown in the PR).
**Update** it on every push (the commit SHA deployed).
Mark **inactive** on teardown.

analogy.title: A sign on the door saying which room the meeting is in
analogy.story: Without it, people wander the halls looking for it.
analogy.breaks: Bots spamming a new comment per push create noise, so update a single comment.

example.title: A sticky comment with GitHub Actions

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: One always-current link on every PR.

code.text:
- uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@v2
  with:
    header: preview
    message: |
      🚀 Preview: https://pr-${{ github.event.number }}.preview.acme.dev
      Commit: ${{ github.sha }}

points: Put the URL in the PR.

check.q: Why update a single sticky comment instead of posting new ones?
check.a: It keeps one current link and avoids flooding the PR with outdated comments.
